name: Chillida Leku
funding: Run by the Chillida estate in partnership with Hauser & Wirth.
records_note: Its site shows sponsorship tiers from 2,000 euros a year but names no funders, and posts no reports, accounts or board.

name: Es Baluard Museu
funding: Govern balear, Consell de Mallorca, Palma council and Fundació d'Art Serra form the foundation. Sponsors: Fundació Baleària, Caixa Colonya, El Corte Inglés, Summum Hotel Group, Hotel Saratoga.
watch: Sponsor names come from the collaborators page. No energy, tobacco, arms or gambling name appears. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2007 to 2025 and accounts 2004 to 2025 with audits, a sponsor logo page, and names its Board of Trustees.

name: Artium Museoa
funding: Basque public museum funded mainly by the Álava provincial council.
records_note: It posts activity reports 2019 to 2025, audited accounts 2019 to 2025, sponsor logos without dates, and names its Patronato.

name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art Sri Lanka
funding: Non-profit set up in 2019, with no fixed venue. Founding Patrons are individuals; the John Keells Foundation was named primary sponsor in March 2020.
watch: John Keells Holdings, the foundation's parent, developed the City of Dreams Sri Lanka resort (opened August 2025); Melco manages the casino with JKH.
records_note: It posts its 2025/26 audit report, names its board, and lists Founding Patrons for 2026; no earlier annual reports are linked.

name: Lunds Konsthall
funding: Municipal kunsthalle run by Lund municipality.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Lund municipality posts annual reports 2024 and 2025 and lists its culture committee; no funder list.

name: Malmö Konsthall
funding: Municipal kunsthalle run by the City of Malmö.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Malmö stad posts its 2025 annual report with accounts; no funder list, no board found.

name: Bildmuseet
funding: University museum of Umeå University, funded by the Swedish state.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2012 to 2022; parent Umeå University posts annual reports 2024 and 2025 and lists its board; no funder list.

name: Kunsthalle Bern
funding: Members, Förderkreise, Berner Kunstfonds, Stiftung Kunsthalle Bern, project foundations.
watch: Published an ethics code June 2026; public subsidy roster not read.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2016 to 2025 with balance sheet and audit report, names funders in the 2025 thanks pages, and lists its board.

name: Kunsthaus Baselland
funding: Canton Basel-Landschaft, Münchenstein, Muttenz, Novartis (long-term partner), Basellandschaftliche Kantonalbank, Habasit, Jenzer Fleisch + Feinkost and a hotel, per the site's logo strip.
watch: Novartis paid $678M in July 2020 to settle US claims that it bribed doctors through speaker programmes. No protest at the Kunsthaus found.
why_flagged: Novartis paid $678M in July 2020 to settle US claims that it bribed doctors through speaker programmes. No protest at the Kunsthaus found.
records_note: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 carry full accounts and a named partner and supporter list; the association board and foundation council are listed.

name: Kunst Halle Sankt Gallen
funding: 2024 income CHF 684k: Stadt St.Gallen 208k, Kanton 196k, other grants 165k (Swisslos, Pro Helvetia, foundations), members and Club der 20 CHF 105k. Raiffeisen funds education.
watch: Club der 20 members include UBS and Helvetia; Julius Bär and Würth are firm friends at CHF 500 to 1,500. Swisslos is a public lottery.
records_note: Annual reports 2016 to 2025 with full accounts, a funder page naming backers year by year to 2026, and a listed board.

name: Juming Museum
funding: Ju Ming Culture and Education Foundation (assets NT$167M, 2020), plus admissions, friends scheme and exhibition sponsors.
watch: Roster not checked. No full funder list published. 2026 show credits Ministry of Culture, InterContinental hotel, a metalwork firm. No controversy found.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2016 to 2025 with CPA-audited statements, a donor thanks page and a named board of nine.

name: National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts
funding: Funded by the Ministry of Culture. 2025 gifts of NT$5.64M came from property and building-materials firms, the E.SUN Foundation (bank), France's CCAC and individuals.
watch: State museum; roster not checked. Some donor names are masked in the filing. In Aug 2026 the Gwangju Biennale renamed its Taiwan Pavilion 'NTMoFA', a row not of the museum's making.
records_note: Annual reports 2017 to 2025, audited final accounts and dated donation lists are on its site; as a state agency it has no board.
